name: Pre-2026 student repos: HliebOcheretianyi/AirAlert_predictions, TeamMLPythonAM2/AirAlarmsApp, shymanskyimarian-ux/air-raid-prediction, sortafreel/dmbm
type: repo (4 student / hobby repos, reviewed together as one peer group)
year: Hlieb: created 2025-03-16, last commit 2025-05-06 (pushed 2025-05-21). TeamML: created 2025-03-17, last commit 2025-05-06 (pushed 2026-01-08). shymanskyi: one-day repo, 2026-06-25 (5 commits; data only to 2022-10-15). dmbm: 2022-09-18 (5 commits, data 2022-02-25..09-15).
authors: Hlieb: HliebOcheretianyi, NoroiMusha37, Merdet, holliban (student team; README clone path 'H2_python_structure_and_data' suggests a university Python/data-science course homework [uncertain]). TeamML: TeamMLPythonAM2 org with VKyl, locde0, kotiksfotikom, Solyariy, kttrryn (student team, same course style [uncertain]). shymanskyi: shymanskyimarian-ux (single author). dmbm: sortafreel (single author).
popularity: Checked 2026-10-17: Hlieb 0 stars, 0 forks; TeamML 2 stars, 1 fork; shymanskyi 0 stars; dmbm 4 stars. No licenses on any of the four.
peer_review_status: student repos / hobby projects; self-reported results only; no peer review. Two of four (shymanskyi, dmbm) report no forecast evaluation at all.
target_type: Hlieb: STATE target (alert active in the hour; start floored and end CEILED to the hour, so every alert covers at least 2 hourly rows), which inflates scores. TeamML: ONSET-like target (is_alarm = 1 if an alert's start falls in that hour [t, t+1)), but evaluated with accuracy and no at-risk mask. shymanskyi: COUNT (daily national alert count, ARIMA) plus a hand-made per-oblast 'will there be an alert' table. dmbm: descriptive only (counts per hour/weekday/month), no target.
target_definition: Hlieb: event_all_region(region, hour h) = 1 if any oblast-level alert interval [floor_h(start), ceil_h(end)] covers h; same-hour label, the 'forecast' for the next 24h is produced by feeding forecast weather for each future hour into the same classifier, so H is implicitly 0..24h with no lag structure. TeamML: is_alarm(city, hour h) = 1 if an alert starts in hour h (alarms joined to the weather grid on floor_h(start)); the app predicts 'probability of an alert for a selected region and N hours ahead' and 'hourly predictions for the next 24h' with hard 0/1 model.predict outputs. shymanskyi: ARIMA(7,1,1) on daily national alert counts, 7-day horizon (code commented out); the shipped weekly table (2022-10-16..22) lists one 'Yes' alert per oblast per day with a probability, start-hour window, duration and threat type, generated outside the repo code. dmbm: none.
spatial_unit: Hlieb: oblast (24 incl. Kyiv City and Crimea in labels; weather by oblast centre city; Kyiv City reuses Kyiv oblast weather). TeamML: oblast via its centre city (24 'city_address' units incl. 'Kyiv oblast'). shymanskyi: national daily count + oblast table. dmbm: oblast (Kyiv City merged into Kyiv region) and Lviv region.
at_risk_masking: None of the four. Hlieb trains and scores on all hours including hours already under alert (the state target makes this the main source of skill). TeamML does not drop hours where the oblast is already under alert; with an onset target that matters less, but there is no mask. shymanskyi/dmbm: not applicable.
data_sources: Hlieb: course-supplied alarms.csv (columns id, region_id, region_city, all_region, start, end; 55,788 oblast-level rows, 2022-02-24 .. 2025-03-01) [uncertain: provenance not stated; looks like the ukrainealarm/air-alarms export used in Ukrainian DS courses]; ISW daily reports scraped from understandingwar.org (2022-02-24 onward); Visual Crossing hourly weather for oblast centre cities (608,304 rows); live alerts.in.ua API for inference; Ukrainian and Russian holiday calendars. TeamML: same style alarms_clean.csv (54,442 rows after dedup on region_city+start), Visual Crossing weather, ISW reports, Telegram channel messages (TF-IDF), live alerts API + weather API + Telegram scraper on AWS EC2 hourly cron. shymanskyi: full_data.csv = 14,480 rows in the Vadimkin official schema (oblast, raion, hromada, level, started_at, finished_at; 10,885 oblast / 878 raion / 2,717 hromada), 2022-03-15 .. 2022-10-15. dmbm: Telegram channel exports (Lviv ODA channel and an all-Ukraine alert channel), 2022-02-25 .. 2022-09-15.
data_source_variant: Hlieb and TeamML: oblast-level only (all_region column; Hlieb even forces all_region 0 -> 1, so any partial-oblast alert is treated as a whole-oblast alert), no raion/hromada union; snapshot ends 2025-03-01, i.e. before the 2025 raion/hromada shift became dominant. Neither uses the Vadimkin official or volunteer file explicitly [uncertain]. shymanskyi: Vadimkin official-format file (subset to Oct 2022), all three levels present but daily counts simply count rows (no union, no dedup). dmbm: raw Telegram channel messages (a volunteer-like channel, closer to Vadimkin's volunteer source than to the official one).
preprocessing: Hlieb: no dedup of alerts (only a later dedup on (timestamp, region_id) of the merged grid: 643,944 -> 622,656 rows); overlapping alerts in the same oblast simply produce duplicate grid rows; median imputation computed on the whole dataset (df.fillna(df.median())) before splitting; label-encoding and StandardScaler fit on the training fold (scaler then saved), but the TF-IDF (2,000 bigrams) + PCA(400, whiten) on ISW text were fit on the full 2022-2025 corpus. Possible timezone misalignment: alarm times are naive (apparently Kyiv local) converted with .timestamp() (treated as UTC) and joined to Visual Crossing true epoch hours, which would shift labels by 2-3 h relative to weather/hour features [uncertain]. TeamML: drop_duplicates(region_city, start); fillna(0) for no-alarm hours; Kyiv oblast weather duplicated from Kyiv; PCA(100) re-fit SEPARATELY on the test fold (pca.fit_transform on X_test), so train and test text features live in different bases. shymanskyi: daily counts of all rows (all admin levels, no dedup, no union), missing days filled with 0. dmbm: regex start/end markers, consecutive duplicate messages collapsed, 4 alarms with no start skipped, first bugged message dropped.
known_label_artefacts: Duplicates: Hlieb never deduplicates alerts; TeamML dedups on (region_city, start); shymanskyi counts raw rows; dmbm collapses repeated Telegram announcements (Lviv alerts are posted 2-3 times). Naive/30-min ends: not discussed by any repo; Hlieb's ceil-to-hour end makes every alert >= 2 positive hours, which inflates state scores further. Standing alerts: not handled (data either ends Oct 2022 or is oblast-level only to Mar 2025, so the long hromada alerts of Kharkivska are absent or partial). Gaps: none detected or masked; the official Aug-Sep 2026 gap is outside all their windows. Swapped columns / timezone: Hlieb and TeamML mix naive local alarm times with epoch-based weather hours without explicit tz handling [uncertain]. Partial-oblast alerts: Hlieb rewrites all_region 0 -> 1 (rewrite_alarms.ipynb), counting partial alerts as whole-oblast. Kyiv City vs oblast: dmbm maps 'м.Київ' to 'Kyiv region' (merges the two units).
model_family: Hlieb: XGBoost, LightGBM (scale_pos_weight), Random Forest (class_weight balanced), Logistic Regression, SGD; final = custom stacking (XGB+RF+LGBM base, LogisticRegression meta, SMOTE on training data) pickled as 3__MUSE__v1. TeamML: LinearRegression and LogisticRegression in the notebook; deployed model = sklearn HistGradientBoostingClassifier v4 (training notebook not in the repo). shymanskyi: statsmodels ARIMA(7,1,1) on daily counts (commented out) + rule-based threat-type table. dmbm: none (descriptive statistics and animated maps).
features: Hlieb (about 1,040 columns): region_id; day_datetimeEpoch and hour_datetimeEpoch (raw time as a trend feature); ~30 Visual Crossing hourly and DAILY weather fields (temp, dew, humidity, precip, wind, pressure, cloudcover, visibility, uvindex, sunrise/sunset, moonphase, conditions, preciptype dummies); 1,000 ISW TF-IDF/PCA components from the previous day's report; event_lastDay_region (number of alert hours on the SAME calendar day, kept in X); ru_holiday, ua_holiday. event_1h_ago, event_2h_ago and alarms_in_regions were built but dropped from X. TeamML (~224 columns): hourly and daily weather; day_hour; dist_from_front (hand-coded 0..1 per city); alarm_num_atm (number of oblasts with an onset in the SAME hour, nationwide); alarm_num_region (onsets in the same oblast on the SAME day); duration_in_min of the alert itself (equal to the label; logistic coefficient 13.2, by far the top feature, later dropped); 100 ISW and 100 Telegram TF-IDF/PCA components shifted +1 day; in production also alarms_hourly (current national alert count), city_hour_score (hard-coded city x hour alarm-rate table) and holiday coefficients. shymanskyi: lags 1-7 of daily count (ARIMA). dmbm: none. No repo uses own-state features like minutes since last start/end or neighbour-oblast state.
external_feature_timing: ISW: Hlieb joins report dated D to every hour of D+1 (date_tomorrow); TeamML shifts ISW and Telegram vectors by +1 day in training (shifting-isw-and-telegram.ipynb) but the first merge notebook joined ISW on the SAME day. ISW reports are typically published late evening US Eastern time, i.e. early morning Kyiv time of D+1 [uncertain exact lag], so a D -> D+1 00:00 join can be a few hours early for the first hours of D+1 (small look-ahead), but most hours are safe. In production TeamML scrapes TODAY's ISW report (ISWScraper.get_full_page_content(today)), which differs from the D-1 lag used in training (train/serve skew), and Hlieb uses the latest available row (tail(1)). Telegram (TeamML): messages per hour shifted by 24h in training; in production the most recent hour of messages is used (lag mismatch). Weather: both teams train on OBSERVED historical weather (an oracle for future hours) plus daily aggregates (day_tempmax, day_precip, ...) that summarise the whole day including hours after t; at inference they use Visual Crossing FORECASTS, so the training skill from weather is not what is available live. Also, the TF-IDF/PCA fits on the full corpus (Hlieb) or on the test set itself (TeamML) are not time-respecting.
ablation_design: None in a controlled sense. Hlieb compares five model families on the same row-index fold but never ablates ISW/weather/holiday groups. TeamML drops leaky columns one at a time inside the same notebook (duration_in_min, alarm_num_atm) without reporting before/after metrics. No repo compares 'with vs without external features' on the same time-restricted sample, so the value of ISW/weather/Telegram is unproven.
split_scheme: Hlieb: sklearn TimeSeriesSplit(n_splits=5) on ROW INDEX, last fold only (518,880 train / 103,776 test). The parquet used was last sorted by ['region_id', 'timestamp'] (feature_2.ipynb), so the 'test' fold is very likely the last ~4 region_ids over the whole 2022-2025 period, not the latest weeks: 103,776 = exactly 4 x 25,944 hourly rows per region [uncertain but strongly indicated]. This is a spatial, not temporal, split. No purge. TeamML: data_split.ipynb sorts by datetime and uses TimeSeriesSplit(n_splits=2) (202,657 / 202,657); model_training.ipynb uses TimeSeriesSplit(3) on merged_all_new.parquet whose ordering is not shown [uncertain]; no purge, no validation slice, no refit protocol. shymanskyi: no split (fit on all data, forecast forward). dmbm: none.
metrics: Hlieb: accuracy, F1, precision/recall (classification_report), confusion matrix at the default 0.5 threshold; weighted F1 for stacking. TeamML: accuracy and confusion matrix (logistic); MAE/MSE/RMSE/R^2 for the linear-regression-on-binary model. No Brier, log loss, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, or calibration in any repo. shymanskyi and dmbm: no metrics.
unit_of_metric: Pooled across all oblasts and hours (Hlieb, TeamML); no within-oblast metrics.
baseline_strength: No explicit baselines anywhere. Implied no-skill baselines show how weak the claims are: TeamML logistic accuracy 0.8999 vs majority-class accuracy 1 - 15,016/151,874 = 0.9011, so it is no better than always predicting 'no alarm'. Hlieb XGBoost accuracy 0.903 vs majority-class 0.826 (17.4% positives in the test fold); but with a state target, persistence (alert active in the previous hour) would very likely beat it, and event_1h_ago was deliberately dropped so this was never measured. No climatology, rolling recent rate, or calibrated persistence.
calibration: None. Hlieb and TeamML ship hard 0/1 predictions (model.predict). The shymanskyi table reports 'probabilities' that look like empirical frequencies k/31 (64.5, 61.3, 90.3, 96.8%) [uncertain], with every row labelled 'Yes'. SMOTE and scale_pos_weight / class_weight='balanced' in Hlieb distort predicted probabilities away from the base rate.
calibration_under_drift: Not examined by any repo. The base rate is pooled 2022-2025 for Hlieb/TeamML; the Jan-2025 drone surge sits at the very end of their data and is not analysed.
uncertainty_of_gain: None: no CIs, bootstrap, or significance tests.
regime_coverage: Hlieb/TeamML: 2022-02-24 .. 2025-03-01, so they include the start of the 2025 drone surge but none of the 2025 raion/hromada reform effects (oblast-level data) and nothing of the Sep-2026 yellow/red reform. Hlieb's test fold is regional, not temporal, so regime change is not tested at all. shymanskyi: Mar-Oct 2022 only (the forecast week 2022-10-16..22 is right after the 10 Oct 2022 missile campaign began). dmbm: Feb-Sep 2022.
leakage_handling: Weak; several concrete leaks. (1) Same-day aggregates: Hlieb event_lastDay_region counts alert hours on the SAME calendar day (includes the target hour and future hours) and stays in X; TeamML alarm_num_region (onsets in the same oblast that day) and alarm_num_atm (national onsets in the same hour) were top features. (2) Target-as-feature: TeamML duration_in_min equals the label (coef 13.2) until dropped. (3) Oracle weather: observed future-hour weather and full-day daily weather aggregates used as features. (4) Full-data fits: median imputation and ISW TF-IDF/PCA fit on all data (Hlieb); PCA refit on the test fold (TeamML); city_hour_score is a hard-coded target encoding probably computed on all data (TeamML) [uncertain]. (5) Split: row-index TimeSeriesSplit on region-sorted rows (Hlieb) means training covers the same hours as test, so cross-oblast same-hour co-occurrence (mass attacks hit many oblasts at once) leaks heavily through shared weather-day/ISW-day features and the timestamp feature. (6) No purge, no truncation test, no negative control. Positive points: both teams dropped event_1h_ago/event_2h_ago and the contemporaneous national count from the final X; TeamML shifted ISW/Telegram by one day; Hlieb applied a D+1 join for ISW.
test_window_hygiene: Poor. Test folds were used for repeated model comparison and feature dropping in notebooks; hyperparameter searches (commented RandomizedSearchCV with TimeSeriesSplit on the train fold) are not separated from the test; no pre-registration, no frozen test date, no record of how many times the test was viewed.
headline_results: Hlieb (test fold of 103,776 rows, 17.4% positive): XGBoost accuracy 0.903, F1 0.681 (precision 0.80, recall 0.59); LightGBM accuracy 0.865, F1 0.671; stacking (SMOTE, weighted metrics) accuracy 0.846, weighted F1 0.858, weighted precision 0.885. These do not beat a persistence baseline in any demonstrated way and are inflated by a state target, same-day leakage and a regional (not temporal) split. TeamML: logistic accuracy 0.8999, which is BELOW the majority-class rate 0.9011 (no skill); linear regression R^2 0.028; deployed HGB model has no reported test metrics. shymanskyi: no evaluation; the weekly forecast table predicts an alert for every oblast every day (168/168 'Yes'), which is trivially true for that period and uninformative. dmbm: descriptive only, e.g. Lviv region averaged 0.97 air alerts per day (Feb-Sep 2022). None of the four shows skill over a naive baseline.
code_available: All four public on GitHub, no license. Hlieb: notebooks + Flask app + pickled models (about 20 MB), data not committed, recommends 32 GB RAM. TeamML: FastAPI backend + React UI + AWS deploy workflow + pickled HGB/TF-IDF/PCA; HGB training notebook missing; CI test.yml present but no real model tests [uncertain]. shymanskyi: single main.py (105 lines) + data CSV; the forecast table is not reproducible from the code. dmbm: notebooks + Telegram exports + processed JSON. None maintained after 2025 except a README push.
takeaways_for_project: (1) State vs onset: Hlieb's state label with ceil-to-hour ends shows exactly why we keep the onset target with the at-risk mask (CLAUDE.md Target section); report persistence on both views only if we want to show the inflation. (2) External features: the ISW/Telegram/weather setups illustrate the publication-lag and oracle risks. If we ever add an ISW feature, use the report for day D only from its actual publication time (conservatively D+1 06:00 Kyiv, then convert to UTC per our rule that grid work is UTC), never full-day weather aggregates, and only forecast (not observed) weather valid at t; any such addition is a new dependency/feature group and needs Oleksandr's approval. (3) Same-day and same-hour aggregates (event_lastDay_region, alarm_num_region, alarm_num_atm) are the dominant leak class; our tests/test_leakage.py truncation test plus its negative control should include a planted 'same calendar day count' feature, since that is the most common real mistake in peer repos. (4) Row-index TimeSeriesSplit on panel data sorted by unit is a silent spatial split; our walk-forward by DATE (D-021, D-023) with purge avoids it. Add an assertion that max(train t) < min(val t) < min(test t) across all units. (5) Fits on full data (median imputation, TF-IDF/PCA, target-encoded city x hour tables) are the 'scalers/encoders fit on full data' forbidden in CLAUDE.md; climatology must be computed from train only, which we already do. (6) Accuracy at 0.5 hides no-skill models (TeamML 0.8999 vs 0.9011 majority); our primary metric BSS vs the rolling recent-rate (D-021) plus PR-AUC/base rate is the right antidote. (7) Treating partial-oblast alerts as whole-oblast (Hlieb all_region 0 -> 1) is consistent with our union rule, but without dedup and the D-020 24h causal cap it would mis-state 2025-2026 data. (8) shymanskyi's file mixes oblast/raion/hromada rows and counts them, a concrete example of why we dedup first and build the per-oblast union. (9) Nothing in these repos contradicts our design; they serve as anti-pattern references for the README's related-work section.
best_practices: Worth adopting: lag text features by at least one publication cycle (TeamML's +1 day shift is the right instinct); keep a live inference path that uses the same feature-timing rules as training (both teams had train/serve skew, a warning for M5/M6); the dedup on (unit, start) and collapse of repeated Telegram announcements (TeamML, dmbm) mirror our dedup-first rule; end-to-end hourly cron deployment (TeamML) is a reference for M6 future work. Anti-patterns to avoid: state targets with ceil-rounded ends; same-day or same-hour aggregate features; using the target's own duration as a feature; observed future weather and full-day daily aggregates as predictors; median imputation or TF-IDF/PCA fit on all data, and PCA refit on the test set; row-index TimeSeriesSplit on unit-sorted panel data; raw timestamps (epoch) as features; SMOTE/class weights without recalibration; hard 0/1 outputs labelled as probabilities; accuracy/F1 at 0.5 as the only metric with no baseline; mixing naive local times with UTC epochs; forecasting 'Yes' for every unit (uninformative); unreproducible forecast tables not produced by the code.
